newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Profit-taking takes shine off India GDR.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Profit-taking takes shine off India GDR.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) slipped on Wednesday, taking their cue from the Bombay market where profit-takers moved in after several days of surging prices, traders said.
"Prices have been consolidating today. It appears that every time the (Bombay) index gets to 4,000 there is serious profit-taking," one trader said.
The Bombay index ended the day 3.62 points lower at 3,940.99 and down from an intraday high 4,029.56.
Prices have risen sharply since last week's Indian budget, which was far more friendly to the market than had been expected.
The HSBC James Capel index now stands at 77.35, off 0.53 percent. The foreign premium fell to 14.84 percent from Tuesday's 15.05 percent.
But price level are still holding near recent highs and traders said they expect support to remain, calling the latest downturn a period of consolidation rather than any change of bullish sentiment.
East India Hotels dipped 30 cents to $19.25, while Bajaj was about steady at $40 and compared to its recent high of $42.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended almost unchanged at 58.55, with a premium of 39.76 percent over the local market, compared with yesterday's 36.77 percent.
The Korea Composite Index finished the day 5.07 points lower at 674.90.
A new high in the Taipei stock market, helped push the Capel Taiwan GDR Index 1.60 points higher by the close to 105.61, with a premium of 0.51 percent compared to Tuesday's 0.40 percent.
The Taiwan Weighted Index closed at a six-year high of 8,019.46, and brokers were predicting enough momentum to hit 8,400.
